John Dos Passos, Manhattan Transfer.
Standard Ebooks edition: https://standardebooks.org/ebooks/john-dos-passos/manhattan-transfer

People whose words are in the text, and their death years:
- John Dos Passos, the author, died 1970.

First publication of the text used: 1925 (SE colophon: 'Manhattan Transfer was published in 1925 by John Dos Passos.')

Why this is public domain:
- United States: the edition's rights statement (quoted below) says the text is in the US public domain. The text was first published in 1925, and a US work from 1925 entered the public domain on 1 January 2021.
- Country of origin: United States. Wikipedia https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manhattan_Transfer_(novel): "an American novel" published in 1925 by Harper & Brothers, with no other country's edition named. The US rule settles the origin for a work first published in the US before 1931, so the text is public domain in its country of origin whatever the death year, and the last person to die (1970) does not change that.

The edition's own statement of rights (from the repository's content.opf):
"The source text and artwork in this ebook are believed to be in the United States public domain; that is, they are believed to be free of copyright restrictions in the United States. They may still be copyrighted in other countries, so users located outside of the United States must check their local laws before using this ebook. The creators of, and contributors to, this ebook dedicate their contributions to the worldwide public domain via the terms in the [CC0 1.0 Universal Public Domain Dedication](https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/zero/1.0/)."
